'''Per-Olof Persson''' is a Swedish-American professor of applied mathematics at [[University of California, Berkeley]], and a mathematician faculty senior scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. His research focuses include numerical methods for partial differential equations, high-order accurate methods, and unstructured mesh generation.

== Education and career ==
Persson holds a Master of Science in engineering physics from [[Lund University]] and completed his Ph.D. in [[applied mathematics]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in 2005.

Following his doctorate, he served as a postdoctoral associate, an instructor of applied mathematics, and a visiting assistant professor of aeronautics and astronautics at MIT.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Persson |first=Per-Olof |date=19 February 2026 |title=Linkedin |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/per-olof-persson-b7a713/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260219202733/https://www.linkedin.com/authwall?trk=gf&trkInfo=AQE_xlUaHp2DAgAAAZx3lhsg4ex8wn1Mfb80XjZjZADds0RoZK_nYnrYwDAcPp1HM6q26tp0YU14fkuRFAjkmizatz2sZOOol-NW535oPbkeP80arQRHs7tVjA5yLV56AVRuHb8=&original_referer=&sessionRedirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fin%2Fper-olof-persson-b7a713%2F |archive-date=19 February 2026 |access-date=19 February 2026 |website=Linkedin}}</ref>

Prior to his academic career, he spent several years developing commercial numerical software for the finite element package [[COMSOL Multiphysics]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Per-Olof Persson, UC Berkeley Mathematics |url=https://persson.berkeley.edu/ |access-date=2026-02-20 |website=persson.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

In 2010, Persson was one of 38 people that were awarded $14 Million for the Air Force Young Investigators Research Program for submitting research proposals that "show exceptional ability and promise for conducting basic research."<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 23, 2009 |title=Air Force awards $14M to 2010 Young Investigators Research Program |url=https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/118755/air-force-awards-14m-to-2010-young-investigators-research-program/ |url-status=live |access-date=February 28, 2026 |website=Air Force}}</ref>

In February 2011, Persson was awarded with the [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] for $50,000 to pursue further research at UC Berkeley.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Four young faculty members to receive $50,000 Sloan Research Fellowships {{!}} Research UC Berkeley |url=https://vcresearch.berkeley.edu/news/four-young-faculty-members-receive-50000-sloan-research-fellowships |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=vcresearch.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

== Research and publications ==

=== Research ===

Persson's research focuses on computational fluid and solid mechanics, with an emphasis on high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods and unstructured mesh generation. In the area of mesh generation, building upon the development of the DistMesh algorithm,<ref>Persson, P.-O.; Strang, G. (2004). "A Simple Mesh Generator in MATLAB". ''SIAM Review''. '''46''' (2): 329–345.</ref> his work extends to space-time and curved meshes. More recently, Persson has introduced machine learning approaches to the field, developing frameworks that utilize deep reinforcement learning and self-play to optimize unstructured triangular and quadrilateral meshes by minimizing irregular nodes.<ref>Narayanan, A.; Pan, Y.; Persson, P.-O. (2024). "Learning topological operations on meshes with application to block decomposition of polygons". ''Computer-Aided Design''. '''175''': 103744.</ref>

Persson has developed numerical discretization schemes designed to improve computational scaling at high polynomial degrees, including the Compact DG scheme,<ref>Peraire, J.; Persson, P.-O. (2008). "The Compact Discontinuous Galerkin (CDG) Method for Elliptic Problems". ''SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing''. '''30''' (4): 1806–1824.</ref> the sparse Line-DG method,<ref>Persson, P.-O. (2013). "A Sparse and High-Order Accurate Line-Based Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Unstructured Meshes". ''Journal of Computational Physics''. '''233''': 414–429.</ref> and half-closed DG methods.<ref>Pan, Y.; Persson, P.-O. (2025). "Half-closed Discontinuous Galerkin discretisations". ''Journal of Computational Physics''. '''524''': 113731.</ref> To address high computational costs associated with high-order methods, his research includes the development of efficient parallel solvers that utilize static condensation, optimally ordered incomplete factorizations by the Minimum Discarded Fill (MDF) method, and Kronecker-SVD preconditioning techniques.<ref>Pazner, W.; Persson, P.-O. (2018). "Approximate tensor-product preconditioners for very high order discontinuous Galerkin methods". ''Journal of Computational Physics''. '''354''': 344–369.</ref>

Persson has also contributed to the development of fully discrete adjoint methods for PDE-constrained optimization, with practical applications such as optimal designs for flapping flight. In collaboration with Matthew Zahr, he developed high-order implicit shock tracking (HOIST) techniques. This approach uses full-space optimization solvers to align curved meshes with flow discontinuities, allowing for the capture of shocks while maintaining high-order convergence.<ref>Zahr, M.; Shi, A.; Persson, P.-O. (2020). "Implicit shock tracking using an optimization-based high-order discontinuous Galerkin method". ''Journal of Computational Physics''. '''410''': 109385.</ref> Additionally, his applied research includes implicit-explicit (IMEX) schemes for partitioned fluid-structure interactions<ref>Froehle, B.; Persson, P.-O. (2014). "A high-order discontinuous Galerkin method for fluid-structure interaction with efficient implicit-explicit time stepping". ''Journal of Computational Physics''. '''272''': 455–470.</ref> and Wall-Resolved [[Large eddy simulation|Large Eddy Simulation]] for turbulent flows.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Per-Olof Persson, UC Berkeley Mathematics |url=https://persson.berkeley.edu/ |access-date=2026-02-20 |website=persson.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

* Peraire, J.; Persson, P.-O. (2008). "The Compact Discontinuous Galerkin (CDG) Method for Elliptic Problems". ''SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing''. '''30''' (4): 1806–1824.

* Persson, P.-O.; Strang, G. (2004). "A Simple Mesh Generator in MATLAB". ''SIAM Review''. '''46''' (2): 329–345.
